market.headline: Tech sold off again on Nvidia's CEO troubles and sticky inflation, but buyers stepped in just above the November lows; the backdrop is still hostile, so buy only what holds its levels.
market.day_type: AI-led selloff that was bought back by the close: QQQ fell as low as 607.76, just above its 20-day low of 606.23, then closed at 633.93, and money moved into bonds for safety, which pulled yields lower.
watch: Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and Friday is a short, thin session, so moves get exaggerated. Don't act in the first hour.
QQQ: a close above 648.00 means the bounce is real; a break of 606.23 means another leg down for every chip stock here.
Dec 1: MRVL earnings (a read on chips), then JOLTS at 10:00; AVGO reports Dec 9 (estimated).

stocks.headline: Fell 3.9% to 149.30 and led the tech selloff; this morning's call: right (it never got back above 150.50).
stocks.why: The business is not the problem. Sales are up 106%, profit forecasts are up 28% in 90 days and the stock is at 8.7x next year's earnings. Investors are selling the person: Huang is back, he refuses to plan for a successor, and federal and state authorities, Congress and shareholders are investigating what Nvidia knew about where Megaspeed's chips ended up. Every day this stays open, it drags MU, TSM, AVGO, ARM, SMCI and CRWV down with it, and it is the main reason QQQ is weak.

long_term.reason: The numbers say Buy, but the investigations can still bring fines, export limits or a forced leadership change, so the low price is not yet a bargain.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A named successor or an investigation closed without charges makes it a Buy; proof that Nvidia knew where the chips went makes it a Trim.
stocks.action: Don't buy Friday's open; add only if it holds above 150.50 after the first hour, and make no new buys at all if it breaks 141.17.

levels.means: above = sellers are done and adding is OK; below = the selling is still in control
above = today's low holds; below = the way is open to the 124.50 low
52-week low; a break means the market is pricing serious legal damage

stocks.headline: Fell 5.1% to 103.88 and set a new 52-week low of 99.34 during the day; this morning's call: right (it never reached 108.24).
stocks.why: Oracle is the market's stand-in for the worry about AI spending: it has a $664.0B backlog of contracts to build for, and higher rates and nervous AI investors make that build-out look expensive. The business itself is speeding up, with sales up 30%, and the stock is at 17x last year's profit, its lowest in five years. The real risk is in the Dec 14 report, where analysts already expect profit per share to drop 16% from a year ago as building costs bite. A weak report there would hit CRWV and the rest of the AI-infrastructure group too.

long_term.reason: This agrees with the house view: fast-growing sales, a record backlog and the cheapest price in five years outweigh the spending worry.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A close below 99.34, or a Dec 14 report showing spending outrunning cash, moves it to Wait.
stocks.action: Don't buy the open; buy a first half-position only if it holds above 99.34 and trades above 105.57 after the first hour, and keep the other half for after the Dec 14 report.

levels.means: above = buyers have taken back today's selloff, so buy the first half; below = stay patient
above = the new low holds; below = no buying until after earnings
above = the drop is fully reversed and the second half can go in before the report

stocks.headline: Fell 4.5% to 601.25 on 1.4x normal volume and is down 38.8% in 20 days; this morning's call: right.
stocks.why: Memory chips are the most cyclical part of the AI trade, and with a beta of 2.00, Micron falls about twice as hard as QQQ whenever Nvidia slips. The business has never looked better: sales are up 345%, the operating margin is 75%, there is a $134.0B backlog, and cash of $38.4B dwarfs debt of $2.8B. Even so, at 2.8x next year's earnings the market is betting this is the peak. The Dec 17 report decides which side is right, and it will move TSM and AVGO with it.

long_term.reason: This agrees with the house view: the business is excellent, but nobody pays for peak profits until the report shows demand is still growing.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A Dec 17 report with a bigger backlog and higher forecasts makes it a Buy.
stocks.action: Don't buy Friday; buy only if it closes back above 622.22, or wait for the Dec 17 report.
